newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian thieves said to stage 'skyway' robbery.
newsitem.headline: Colombian thieves said to stage 'skyway' robbery.

text.p: The pilot of a helicopter laden with more than $500,000 in cash told police he was shot down and robbed on Thursday on the eastern outskirts of Bogota.

The unusual "skyway" robbery was reported by Col. Alonso Arango, National Police commander in Cundinamarca province of which Bogota is the capital, who said the pilot and two crew members aboard the Hughes 500 aircraft claimed to have been shot down by suspected leftist guerrillas shortly after takeoff from the city's El Dorado airport.

Arango, who spoke in an interview with the Radionet news network, said the helicopter was hit by four gunshots, apparently just moments before it crash-landed on a farm in La Calera, a town just across the Andean mountains that ring eastern Bogota.

Arango said the pilot and his crew members were being held for questioning, however, pending an investigation into whether or not the gunshots caused sufficient damage to force the helicopter to land.
"They were shot down according to their version," Arango said. "But we have to study this case a bit closer."

He added that the thieves, who may or may not have been working in collusion with the helcopter crew, made off with $530,000 from the state-run Caja Agraria bank that had been earmarked for shipment to three towns in southern Caquatea province.
